edges.description: Focal venous infarction and lobar parenchymal injury can be complicated by parenchymal bleeding.
Focal venous infarction produces local neurological deficits such as hemiparesis.
Raised intracranial pressure from an obstructed venous system manifests clinically as intracranial hypertension syndrome.
Raised intracranial pressure from cerebral venous sinus thrombosis commonly presents with headache.
Raised intracranial pressure from an obstructed venous system causes papilledema.
Severe cerebral venous thrombosis and intracranial hypertension can progress to encephalopathy and loss of consciousness.
Hemorrhagic venous infarction and lobar parenchymal injury manifest clinically as cerebral hemorrhage.
Cortical and lobar hemorrhagic venous lesions in superior sagittal sinus thrombosis predispose to acute and secondary seizures.
Oral contraceptive use acts as a prothrombotic risk factor promoting dural sinus thrombus formation.
